subject: Beacon demo recap — model slate, benchmarks and procurement path
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir@beaconhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Beacon demo recap — model slate, benchmarks and procurement path

Samir — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written recap and recommended slate so we have a single place to iterate. I pulled the initial microbenchmarks from our runner and attached a small prompt pack you can run locally.

What we demoed
- Live assistant flow (clinical triage + summary) with context window up to 4k tokens
- Two candidate models and a fallback path for cost-sensitive routes

Recommended short list (tradeoffs at a glance)
1) ruby-13b-8bit (quantized) — our primary reco
   - Quality: strongest at multi-turn summarization and preserving clinical context
   - Latency: median generation ~220ms token, P95 ~460ms (on ada-gen-optimized GPU profile)
   - Cost: ~1.1x on per-token relative to pebble-7b but fewer tokens to edit in post-processing
   - When to use: clinician-facing summaries, notes generation, anything where hallucination risk must be lowest

2) pebble-7b-int8 — cost-balanced production model
   - Quality: good for short answers and triage classification (intent extraction)
   - Latency: median ~120ms token, P95 ~260ms
   - Cost: ~0.5x relative to ruby-13b-8bit
   - When to use: high-volume triage, quick inline suggestions, chat UI where cost sensitive

3) fallback: micro-llm-2 (cpu, tiny)
   - Quality: degraded for long-form but acceptable for single-turn lookups
   - Latency: variable, used only for non-critical low-cost fallbacks

Benchmarks and artifacts- Attached: benchmarks_20280514.csv (loads of runner metrics), beacon_prompt_pack_v1.zip (30 representative prompts you shared), mutual_action_plan_beacon_v1.pdf (proposed timeline).
- Eval runner: https://redwood-internal.example.com/eval-runner/BEA-2028-045
- Shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-beacon-eval

Primary risks / quality notes- Clinical hallucinations on rare named-entity sequences — we recommend an automated factuality filter + retrieval augmentation for discharge summaries.- Tokenization edge cases on scanned document OCR; we'll pair with a short normalization preprocessor.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan)
1) Beacon: sign off on prompt pack + allow 48-hour eval against a 5k prompt holdout (we'll host runner).
2) Redwood: run A/B batch (ruby-13b-8bit vs pebble-7b-int8) on your prompts, surface P50/P95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, and hallucination incidents by prompt type.
3) Joint call: security + procurement kickoff (suggest May 18 or 19) to go over SOC2, data residency, and contract timeline.

Can you confirm 48-hour eval permission and which of the two dates work for the security/procurement session?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
Attach: beacon_prompt_pack_v1.zip; benchmarks_20280514.csv; mutual_action_plan_beacon_v1.pdf

From: Samir Khan <samir@beaconhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Beacon demo recap — model slate, benchmarks and procurement path

Ben — appreciate the detailed recap and the artifacts. A few quick clarifying questions before we greenlight the 48-hour run: 

1) Can you share the P99 latency numbers for ruby-13b-8bit and pebble-7b-int8 on the hardware profile you used? P95 is useful but P99 will determine our SLA planning.
2) We need SOC2 evidence and a short note on customer data handling for the eval runner. Is that something you can share ahead of the security call?
3) Hallucination mitigations: you mentioned a factuality filter. Do you have examples of false-positive/false-negative rates from prior clinical evals? Also curious about a recommended pattern for manual review sampling.
4) Cost: ballpark monthly run-rate for ~1M tokens / month across a mixed workload (60% triage short responses, 40% summaries). Can you provide est. cost delta between the two candidate models?

Procurement wants the timeline for contract signature if we decide to proceed — we currently aim to finish vendor selection by June 1. If the 48-hour eval looks good we will move quickly.

Thanks,
Samir Khan
Director, Clinical Systems
Beacon Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Beacon demo recap — model slate, benchmarks and procurement path

Ben / Karthik — quick internal note to answer Samir's P99 ask and to propose the regression plan. Pulling the two candidate rows from the runner: see attached CSV for full traces. Key numbers (same hardware profile used in demo):
- ruby-13b-8bit: P50 token 220ms, P95 token 460ms, P99 token 820ms
- pebble-7b-int8: P50 token 120ms, P95 token 260ms, P99 token 520ms

Cost estimate (rough, using their projected mix ~1M tokens/mo):
- ruby-13b-8bit: ~$14,500 / month (includes memory + GPU time + infra overhead)
- pebble-7b-int8: ~$7,900 / month

Hallucination / factuality notes- From prior clinical evals: ruby family shows ~2.4% factuality failures on long-form discharge-like prompts without retrieval augmentation; pebble-7b-int8 shows ~5.7% on same set. These are pre-filtered numbers and depend heavily on prompt engineering and retrieval coverage. We'll include the short factuality filter we discussed as part of the eval runner.

Proposed regression plan:
1) Run 48-hour batch A/B with 10k holdout prompts and automated hallucination detector + sample manual review (50 positives / 50 negatives).
2) Return: P50/P95/P99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, hallucination rate by prompt bucket, and a short change log of errors.
3) If ruby passes a 98% acceptance threshold on critical-scenario prompts, propose pilot (2-week) with canary traffic to validate in-prod signals.

I'll attach the bench CSV and the mutual action plan to customer-ready email once Ben confirms.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Attach: benchmarks_20280514.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir@beaconhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, procurement@beaconhealth.com
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Beacon demo recap — model slate, benchmarks and procurement path

Samir — great questions, thank you. Short answers below and a proposal for next steps.

P99 and SLA implications- See the attached benchmarks_20280514.csv — P99 numbers are included. Operationally, we see spike-related P99s during long context generation; our recommended SLA buffer is +20% on observed P99 for planning headroom. We'll include autoscale guardrails for critical routes.

SOC2 and data handling- We'll send the SOC2 Type II report and a short data handling one-pager to your security contact ahead of the call. For the 48-hour eval, customer data stays encrypted in transit and at rest; we spin ephemeral evaluation containers and delete artifacts after 30 days unless you ask for longer retention. I'll loop in security on the calendar.

Hallucination mitigation recommendations- 1) Retrieval augmentation for summaries (connect to your internal KB via ephemeral vector store), 2) Post-generation factuality filter (we'll share the filter's precision/recall curves from prior clinical runs), 3) Manual sampling cadence: start at 1% of production summaries for the first 2 weeks and escalate to 0.5% if stability is good.

Cost estimate recap (1M tokens / mo)
- ruby-13b-8bit: ~$14.5k / mo
- pebble-7b-int8: ~$7.9k / mo
(we'll produce a line-item quote for procurement once you pick the primary model and expected retention/throughput)

Proposed immediate next steps- Can we do the security/procurement kickoff on May 19, 10am PT? Suggested attendees: Samir, one procurement rep, our Head of Security (sec@redwood.ai), Marissa (solutions), and me. I'll send a calendar invite and attach SOC2 + MOP.
- Start 48-hour eval as soon as Samir confirms OK for us to run against the provided prompt pack (we'll keep data isolated).

Links / artifacts (again)
- Eval runner: https://redwood-internal.example.com/eval-runner/BEA-2028-045
- Prompt pack: attached (beacon_prompt_pack_v1.zip)
- Bench CSV: attached (benchmarks_20280514.csv)
- Mutual action plan: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-beacon-eval

If May 19 works I'll add the invite and security docs. Thanks — excited to move this forward.

Ben Carter
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
